structure.title: Letters around a confession
structure.text: Walton's Arctic letters contain Victor's account. The reader encounters an ambitious listener before hearing the ambitious man he admires.

structure.title: A voice within a voice
structure.text: The creature's account enters Victor's narrative, before the enclosing voices resume. Each speaker asks someone else to understand him.

people.name: Victor Frankenstein
people.text: A gifted young Genevan who becomes obsessed with discovering the secret of life, and works alone in his rooms at university to master it.

people.name: The creature
people.text: The being Victor makes, who wakes alone and must learn to speak, read and understand what he is, mostly by watching others.

people.name: Robert Walton
people.text: A young English explorer bound for the North Pole, whose letters to his sister frame the whole story and who shares Victor's ambition.

context.title: Creation and care
context.text: Victor's achievement creates a dependent being. The novel follows needs that discovering a scientific technique does not itself answer.

passages.quote: I might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing

context.title: Paradise Lost
context.text: Milton's account of creation and rebellion gives the creature language for thinking about his maker. No prior reading is required.
context.takeaway: Literary models help him describe his position.

notice.why: Being allowed to speak changes the apparent balance of responsibility.

notice.text: Compare admiration with acts of care.
notice.why: Grand ambitions can coexist with neglected immediate obligations.

opening: Victor Frankenstein dreams of a species that will love and bless him. He works in secret, neglects his family, and discovers how to create life, only to flee when the being he has made opens its eyes. Abandoned, the creature learns to speak and watches a family offer one another the affection he wants for himself. When he finally finds Victor, he can explain what his creator has done to him, and the scientist who wanted gratitude must answer a demand.
